subject: yogis
one_liner: The pose distribution platform. Browse 4,000+ asanas, buy them during seasonal sales, and get to them eventually.
brand_voice_notes: Storefront UI language applied to the human body, delivered flat. Patch-note cadence. Discounts stated as spiritual events. Prices stated with confidence and never justified. Review-culture vocabulary (Overwhelmingly Positive, Mostly Negative, Verified Owner) used as if it were scripture. The word 'wellness' never appears.

hero.h1: Own every pose. Do four of them.
hero.sub: Drishti is the world's largest digital pose storefront. Build a library of over 4,000 asanas, install them into your body at your own pace, and leave reviews for the ones you never opened.

features.title: Your Backlog
features.blurb: Every pose you buy goes straight to your library, where it stays. Drishti tracks hours practiced with two-decimal honesty, so you always know Pigeon Pose has been in your body for 14 months and run for 0.2 hours.

features.title: Early Access Asanas
features.blurb: Practice poses before they're finished. Headstand is currently in version 0.4 and ships without neck support. Weekly patch notes tell your hamstrings exactly what changed and what is still a known issue.

features.title: Verified Reviews
features.blurb: Every pose is reviewed by people who did it once. Savasana holds Overwhelmingly Positive at 98%. Chair Pose has been Mostly Negative since 2019, and the developers have stopped responding.

perks: Patch notes delivered to your mat

demo_screen_concept: A Steam-style library view for owned poses. Left sidebar: searchable list of owned asanas with per-pose hours practiced (mostly 0.0), sortable by hours or recency. Main pane: the selected pose's store-page detail with capsule art, review verdict (Savasana: Overwhelmingly Positive; Chair Pose: Mostly Negative), a review histogram, tag chips (Relaxing, Difficult, Early Access, Floor-Based), locked and unlocked achievements, latest patch notes, and a 'Practice Now' button that runs a fake install progress bar labeled 'Installing into hamstrings…' and always stalls at 91% before completing.

images.rationale: Demo is photo-shaped (pose capsule art, like game covers), so the budget went to capsules: one hero Featured & Recommended capsule (crow) plus three library capsules (savasana, headstand, chair) reused across landing and demo. Testimonial headshots skipped so all three review cards keep consistent initials badges.

design_direction.style: Game-storefront library console, incense-dark slate mode. The page is staged as the storefront of a heavily funded digital distribution company that has decided the human body is a launcher and sells stillness by the unit. A flat incense-dark slate blue ground (#151C26) runs the whole page with no gradients and no glow; panels are store capsules: flat fills one shade lighter than the ground (#1C2634), 1px hairline borders (#2A3648), 8px radii, no shadows, no glass, no blur; depth comes entirely from capsule layering and the two rationed accents. The core motif is the discount corner tag: a matcha-green (#A9BE55) rectangular tag reading -66% or SOLSTICE SALE, clipped onto capsule corners, pricing rows, and one word per headline, so every serene object on the page is also on sale. The second motif is the review bar: thin horizontal histogram bars in tranquil blue that fill on scroll, summarizing each pose's public opinion with storefront verdicts (Overwhelmingly Positive, Mostly Negative) set in small caps. Metadata chrome annotates everything: tag chips (RELAXING, DIFFICULT, EARLY ACCESS, FLOOR-BASED), hours-played counters, build numbers (Headstand 0.4.2), and Verified Owner badges. One tranquil steam blue (#5FA8D3) carries the wordmark, every primary CTA, links, and positive review bars; the matcha green appears strictly on discount tags and Overwhelmingly Positive verdicts, and nowhere else. Marcellus sets the wordmark and headlines in Roman inscriptional serif caps, carved-studio-signage calm over storefront machinery; Inter carries plain, faintly platform-TOS body copy. Every figure that pretends to be library telemetry (hours practiced, backlog counts, discount percentages, tier prices) is set in Space Mono with tabular figures inside inset slate wells, so it reads like the client, not marketing. Motion is storefront-restrained: capsules lift 3px on hover with the border brightening, discount tags tick in once with a small rotation settle, review bars fill once on scroll, CTAs depress 1px on press, sections fade up 6px with a 40ms stagger, all gated behind prefers-reduced-motion. No light mode, no glass, no blur panels, no neon glow, no clay, no bento lattice, no didone engraving, no condensed athletic type, no HUD brackets, no sign-painter rounding, no emoji. Reads like a company that files inner peace under 'seasonal content' and considers your body a storage limitation.
design_direction.archetype: Digital storefront landing: split hero with inscriptional headline left and a Featured & Recommended pose capsule right (discount tag, review bar, tag chips), seasonal sale strip, three feature capsules, testimonial review cards with Verified Owner badges, pricing as editions ladder, closing CTA band, handoff to the library demo.
design_direction.motion_vocab: Capsule hover lift 3px with border brighten, discount tags tick in with a rotation settle, review bars fill once on scroll, CTAs depress 1px on press, sections fade up 6px with 40ms stagger, all gated behind prefers-reduced-motion.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Split hero. Left: Marcellus inscriptional headline with one matcha-tagged word, platform-TOS sub, one steam-blue CTA plus a ghost 'open the demo' link. Right: a Featured & Recommended capsule for Crow Pose with capsule art, a -66% Solstice Sale corner tag, price row ($2.31 struck from $6.79), review histogram, and tag chips.
